intelligence.enrichment: Liquids and gases are fluids because they flow and do not retain a fixed shape; solids are distinguished from them by retaining a definite shape. ability to flow and lack of fixed shape -> classification as a fluid The learner classifies liquids and gases as fluids because they flow and lack fixed shape, while solids are not fluids merely because many grains can be poured. Anything that can be poured is a liquid or fluid, even if it is made of many solid grains.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Particulate nature of matter. The student must decide: Decide when a substance should be classified as a fluid rather than as a solid. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. Recalculate the key; do not copy source.key. Every option must be a claim that could answer the stem, and wrong options must be the same kind of answer as the key (a next term, a named process, or a row of the same shape). If the stem continues a number list, every option names a next term. Never write that naming or writing a term is what creates the list. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.
